verdict.rationale: FireHydrant's API reference states the API can do "anything you can do on the FireHydrant UI". API keys default to Owner permissions and "can perform actions like any other user", and the published OpenAPI spec spans the API surface, from Call Routes and Permissions to Roles and Audit Events. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of UI/API parity, and feature-by-feature confirmation that UI-specific features (e.g., AI retrospective drafting, Slack-driven runbook actions) are exposed via the API.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: You can use the FireHydrant API to configure integrations, define incidents, and set up webhooks--anything you can do on the FireHydrant UI.
An API key can perform actions like any other user, and by default, it will have Owner permissions.
with operation tags across Call Routes, Permissions, Roles, Audit Events and the rest of the API surface.
